mods.name: DFast
mods.description: Frame-time HUD with p99 and 1%/0.1% lows, a repeatable Bench Mode, and JVM launcher advice matched to your Java version and RAM. Leaves render-ahead control to Sodium when it is installed.

releases.notes:
DFast 0.2.0 turns DFast into a measuring tool you can trust: a frame-time HUD that stays out of the way, and a repeatable benchmark that writes its results to disk.

## For players

- **Frame-time HUD (F9)** — FPS averaged over the last 5 s, the last frame time and p99 frame time, the 1% and 0.1% lows over up to 60 s, and which mod controls render-ahead. Each line shows the span it really covers. Only real gameplay frames are counted: menus, loading overlays, pauses and alt-tab never show up as stutter, but genuine hitches do. The HUD is redrawn four times a second into a texture, so it costs one textured quad per frame and allocates nothing per frame (checked with JFR in the game).
- **Bench Mode** — start the game with `-Ddfast.bench=short` (or `ci`, `long`). DFast opens or creates a fixed-seed world, flies the same camera path every time, measures every frame uncapped, writes `dfast/bench/<run>/result.json`, `system.json` and `frametimes.txt`, and quits. Your own video settings are restored afterwards. `system.json` records your hardware, driver, video settings and mod list, with no file paths or user names.
- **Render-ahead** — with Sodium, Sodium stays in charge. Without Sodium, DFast's experimental one-frame limiter stays **off**: measured on an RTX 4060 laptop (8 interleaved runs per setting), it lowered the 1% low by 15%. Its effect on input latency cannot be measured yet (planned for 0.4.0 with PresentMon).

## For modpack authors and testers

- `tools/bench_compare.py` compares two setups with a 95% Welch t confidence interval and the smallest difference the runs can detect. It needs at least 5 runs per setup and rejects runs that failed, generated the world, overflowed, or ran with a different power source, refresh rate, fullscreen state, GPU or resolution. On the development laptop, 8 runs per setup detect differences of about 10 to 12%.
- CI runs the real client under Linux with Java 21 and 25, alone and with Sodium 0.6.13 and 0.8.13, before any release is published.

## Requirements

Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API 0.116.13+, Java 21+.

## Known limits

- Input-to-photon latency is not measured yet.
- If you use Bench Mode on a slow machine, the world save at exit can take a long time; this release waits for it. The next release adds a watchdog that ends the process two minutes after the results are written.

DFast is developed with AI assistance (Claude); every change is reviewed and tested before release. License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with the DonQuaan Addendum.

releases.notes:
**Hotfix for 0.2.0-beta.2. Everyone on beta.1 or beta.2 should update.**

### Fixed
- **JVM advice could stop Java 21 from starting.** beta.2 could suggest `-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders`, which Java 21 rejects. Advice now follows your Java version: Compact Object Headers only on Java 24–26, `-XX:+ZGenerational` only on Java 21–22, and a heap size matched to your RAM (never more than half of it).
- **RAM was never detected** (always reported as -1). It is now read correctly and rounded to the nearest GiB.
- **Render-ahead now has one owner.** With Sodium installed, DFast leaves the CPU render-ahead limit to Sodium and runs no fence loop of its own. Without Sodium, DFast's experimental limiter is **off by default**. beta.1/beta.2 wrote `renderQueueLimiter=true` into every config automatically; that value is reset once when the config is migrated.
- **Minecraft version is enforced.** DFast now requires exactly Minecraft 1.21.1 and Fabric API 0.116.13 or newer instead of loading on any 1.21.x and failing later.
- Removed the missing mod icon and the empty mixin config.

### Changed
- Diagnostics (hardware, JVM advice, render-ahead owner) go to `.minecraft/dfast/dfast.log`; `latest.log` gets one line.
- Config files are written atomically, without comments, and are never overwritten when they cannot be read.
- The HUD (F9) uses the same number format in every language and refreshes its text 4 times per second. Vietnamese translation added.
- Only the mod jar is attached to releases (no sources jar that could be dropped into `mods/` by mistake).

### Known limitation
The experimental limiter (only when you enable it without Sodium) still waits inside the HUD callback. It moves to a proper start-of-frame hook, with measurements, in 0.4.0.

### Verified
84 unit tests (mutation check 8/8), CI on Linux, and the client started on Windows with DFast alone and with Sodium 0.6.13.

DFast is developed with AI assistance; every change is reviewed and tested before release.
